label: Juba and Shabelle basins

location.note: the centre of the box we measured, NOT a place anything was observed. On a catchment it may sit on high ground with no river beneath it.

event_corroboration.source: FAO SWALIM FRRIMS river gauge, Jowhar (Shabelle)
event_corroboration.detail: Jowhar read 5.37 to 5.38 m on 13 to 15 Oct 2026, above SWALIM's high flood-risk level (5.25 m) and 12 cm below bankfull (5.50 m); no primary report of flooding found as of 23 Oct
event_corroboration.note: This channel's own instruments measure rainfall and flood extent. Neither establishes that a flood occurred, so this field carries evidence from outside them and is not derived from anything above.

instrument_coverage.note: the rainfall instrument holds data to 2026-10-21, past the window end of 2026-10-21, so this window is complete

series.units: mm, area mean over the region
no_baseline_reason: the rainfall baseline file holds no year with a complete window, so there is nothing to compare this period against

series.measures: standing water outside the reference water mask
series.present_may_exceed_due_because: due_slots is computed from a conservative 3-day composite latency. When the product publishes sooner, present legitimately exceeds due. A validator asserting present <= due would fail this series for being correct.

notes: The flooded area is likely an undercount: on 13 to 19 October, when the Shabelle at Jowhar peaked, cloud let the satellite see only 52 to 74 percent of the region, and those days read almost no flooding. A day the satellite could not see is not a dry day.
Rainfall is not ranked here: satellite rainfall may only point where to look (D-322), and no same-window rainfall baseline exists for this region.
Attribution: ENSO-loaded window, per the science desk's ruling of 23 Oct 2026 (October to December short rains; IRI El Nino rainfall composites). The tag claims the season's odds, not this flood.
